english.title: Making a gaming machine available for use - Gambling Act 2005
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) made a gaming machine available for use by another other than in accordance with an operating licence issued under section 65(1) of the Gambling Act 2005 or an exception under that Act
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 242(1) and 246(1) of the Gambling Act 2005.

english.notes:
(i) Section 242(1)(b) of the Gambling Act 2005 provides exceptions to this offence created by sections 247, 248, 249, 271, 273, 282, 283 or 287 of that Act where the gaming machine is made available for use in accordance with specific permits etc.
(ii) It is also an offence to make a gaming machine available for use if the machine does not comply with regulations made by the Secretary of State under section 240 of the Gambling Act 2005, see offence wording GA05052/H8231.
(iii) It is a separate offence for a person to use premises for making a gaming machine available for use without the necessary authorisation or exemption, such as a premises licence or a Category D gaming machine permit (section 137(1)(c) of the Gambling Act 2005, see offence wordings GA05002/H8181, GA05003/H8182 and GA05004/H8183).
(iv) For the territorial application of this section see section 251 of the Gambling Act 2005.
(v) A licensing authority may institute criminal proceedings in respect of this offence, section 346(1) of the Gambling Act 2005.

other.penalty:
Fifty one weeks imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level five of the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
12 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
